title: Enabling On-Device Large Language Model Personalization with Self-Supervised Data Selection and Synthesis
problem: Edge devices need to personalize LLMs using sparse user feedback without uploading private data to the cloud, while facing severe storage constraints that prevent large-scale fine-tuning with full user-generated datasets.
motivation: On-device LLM personalization enables user-specific responses in real-time while preserving privacy and minimizing annotation burden on users.
method: The system automatically identifies and stores only the most representative training examples from incoming data, reducing memory usage. It then uses the model itself to generate multiple variations of questions and answers from the sparse user feedback, expanding what it can learn from. Finally, it tunes the model directly on your device using this curated dataset, asking the user for more feedback only when needed.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining automatic selection of the most useful training examples with having the model generate its own training variations, making it practical to personalize language models on devices with very limited memory and user feedback.
contributions: First on-device LLM personalization framework addressing privacy and storage constraints
Self-supervised data selection method to identify representative examples with minimal storage footprint
LLM-based semantic data generation to enhance fine-tuning quality with sparse annotations
Demonstrated superior accuracy and fine-tuning speed compared to vanilla baselines
